title: k6 Load Testing Flow
summary: A k6 script spawns virtual users against a target, records metrics like p95 latency, enforces thresholds and streams results to Prometheus and Grafana.

nodes.label: Test Script
nodes.detail: Defines requests, checks and options such as stages, scenarios and thresholds. Stored in Git and run from CI.

nodes.label: k6 Runner
nodes.detail: Executes the script and schedules virtual users. Each VU runs the default function in a loop.

nodes.label: Virtual Users
nodes.detail: Simulated users running in parallel. Ramping stages increase or decrease the VU count over time.

nodes.label: Target Service
nodes.detail: The service or environment receiving the load, ideally a production-like staging setup.

nodes.label: Metrics
nodes.detail: Built-in metrics include http_req_duration, http_req_failed and iterations. Trends report percentiles such as p95.

nodes.label: Thresholds
nodes.detail: Rules like p(95)<500 or error rate under 1 percent. A breach makes k6 exit non-zero, failing the CI job.

nodes.label: Prometheus
nodes.detail: Receives k6 metrics through the Prometheus remote write output for storage next to system metrics.

nodes.label: Grafana
nodes.detail: Plots latency percentiles, request rate and errors, correlated with server-side metrics.

steps.title: Script defines the test
steps.text: The script sets stages, checks and thresholds, and k6 starts it locally or in CI.

steps.title: VUs generate load
steps.text: k6 ramps virtual users that loop through the scenario against the target service.

steps.title: Metrics are recorded
steps.text: Each request is timed; http_req_duration and failure rates are aggregated.

steps.title: Thresholds decide pass/fail
steps.text: k6 compares p95 latency and error rate to limits and exits non-zero on breach.

steps.title: Results are visualised
steps.text: Metrics are remote-written to Prometheus and plotted in Grafana alongside server metrics.
